idiom_name: hand-written base64url cursor + keyset predicate over libpq / sqlite3
implementation_notes: C has no pagination support anywhere in its stack, so the three classical roles are written by hand: a token codec (RFC 4648 base64url over the last row's ordering keys, ideally HMAC-protected), a keyset statement such as SELECT ... WHERE (created_at, id) < ($1, $2) ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT $3, and a page assembler. Bind the cursor values with PQexecParams's parameter arrays (never by formatting them into the SQL text), or compile the same statement once with sqlite3_prepare_v2 and re-bind it per page with sqlite3_bind_int64 / sqlite3_reset while stepping with sqlite3_step until SQLITE_DONE. Fetch page_size + 1 rows to learn whether another page exists; the classic hand-written form is justified because there is no library to delegate to, but it should live in one small module shared by every list endpoint.
pitfalls: The seek predicate must be strict ((created_at, id) < (...), not <=): an inclusive comparison repeats the anchor row on every page and the client never terminates.

64-bit keys must be bound with the right type: sqlite3_bind_int truncates ids where sqlite3_bind_int64 does not, and libpq binary parameters must be host-to-network converted (htonll) with a matching length array.
